causal_chain: A small bank of persistent user preference states can separately store distinct collaborative intents extracted from the user's training interactions.
Because full-sort ranking must distinguish hard positives from nearby substitutes, candidate-specific state selection should recover held-out items that are diluted under single-vector scoring.
Item-conditioned routing over those states lets each candidate be compared against the most relevant latent intent instead of an averaged preference vector.
State transport over the user's observed training-time interaction order preserves which intents co-activate and how later interactions refine earlier ones.
Therefore a multi-state transport recommender should improve NDCG@10 over a matched single-state pairwise control, especially for users with diverse histories.
Users with mixed-taste histories are poorly summarized by a single static embedding.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any observed gain may come from increased parameter count or generic regularization from attention-style pooling rather than from persistent multi-state transport and candidate-conditioned routing.
discriminative_predictions: If transport is causal, ablating chronological state updates while keeping the same number of states and parameters should hurt more on users with longer histories than on short-history users.
Relative improvement should be larger for users whose training histories are more interaction-diverse than for users with narrow homogeneous histories.
Replacing candidate-conditioned routing with uniform averaging over states should substantially reduce or erase any gain if routing is the real mechanism.
expected_evidence: A matched single-state control under the same pairwise protocol underperforms the multi-state transport model on full-sort NDCG@10.
Mechanism-off ablations localize the effect: both no-routing and no-transport variants lose most of the frontier model's advantage.
User-stratified evaluation shows the largest deltas in medium/high diversity history buckets rather than only in head-popularity buckets.
blind_projection.falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if the multi-state transport model fails to beat its matched single-state control, or if any gain remains unchanged after removing candidate-conditioned routing and chronological state transport, indicating the proposed mechanism is not carrying the effect.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This candidate changes the core user representation from one static embedding to a set of persistent latent states, changes the interaction structure by making scoring candidate-conditioned through routing, and adds a custom train-time state transport capability over each user's observed history. These are not parameter tweaks or wrappers around the active profile families.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender that represents each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states, updates those states by train-history transport, and scores each item through candidate-conditioned routing over the state bank will achieve better full-sort NDCG@10 than matched single-state pairwise collaborative filtering because it can preserve and selectively activate distinct intents instead of collapsing them into one average user vector.
implementation_requirements: Build per-user chronologically ordered training histories from the frozen training split.
For each training pair (user, positive item, negative item), compute routed scores by attending from the candidate item embedding to the user's state bank.
Implement a RecBole GeneralRecommender in PyTorch using only train interactions.
Learn item embeddings and K user state slots shared through a state-update module that transports information across observed user events.
Optimize a pairwise ranking loss over routed positive and negative scores.
Provide executable ablations for mechanism-off variants with identical data access and evaluation path.
Support full-sort prediction by computing candidate-conditioned routing for all items at evaluation time.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use a candidate-local matched control with the same item embedding backbone, similar parameter budget, and the same pairwise loss, but collapse the user representation to a single pooled embedding without persistent multi-state slots, candidate-conditioned routing, or chronological transport.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Replace static user scoring with a multi-state user memory architecture: each user owns K latent preference states initialized from train-history aggregation, states are updated by a learned transport operator over the user's observed interaction order, and each candidate item scores by routing attention over the states before computing affinity.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Executable mechanism-off ablation: keep the same item embeddings, pairwise loss, and overall parameter budget, but replace the K-state transport-and-routing user module with a single pooled user embedding computed from the same training history; score items only by direct dot-product between that pooled embedding and item embeddings. Secondary ablation: retain K states but force uniform routing and remove chronological transport updates.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: The smallest isolatable wedge is candidate-conditioned routing over a fixed-size bank of persistent user states built from training histories, compared against the same backbone with one pooled user embedding and no routing.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does persistent multi-state user memory with candidate-conditioned routing provide ranking benefit beyond what a matched single-state collaborative filter can achieve?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: A compact implementation with small K and shallow transport should fit the development budget because ML-1M is modest in size; the main risk is full-sort inference cost from per-item routing, but batched matrix operations should keep qualification within the stated wall and GPU limits.
